item.title: Optimal text-based time-series indices
item.description: The most recent methodological instalment of the sentometrics programme: rather than selecting among pre-specified index constructions, the index itself is optimised for the series it is meant to explain.

item.title: The R package sentometrics to compute, aggregate, and predict with textual sentiment
item.description:
Textual sentiment can be computed in many ways, and pooled into a time series in many more. The package treats that multiplicity as the problem to be solved rather than a nuisance: it computes sentiment, generates many candidate aggregation schemes, and selects among them within the prediction step.

See the package site.

item.title: Sentiment and Econometrics: Toward a Unified Framework of Textual Sentiment Analysis for Economic and Financial Applications
item.description: Supervised by David Ardia and Kris Boudt. Samuel is the author and maintainer of the sentometrics R package.

item.title: Econometrics meets sentiment: An overview of methodology and applications
item.description:
The reference entry point to sentometrics. It walks through the full chain of an econometric analysis of textual sentiment — corpus construction, sentiment computation, aggregation into time series, and use in a model — and organises the applications across economics, finance and politics.

Start here, then read the software vignette.

item.title: Questioning the news about economic growth: Sparse forecasting using thousands of news-based sentiment values
item.description:
Rather than committing to one way of turning news into a sentiment index, the paper generates thousands of candidate indices and lets a sparse regression select the ones that forecast. Winner of the International Journal of Forecasting best paper award 2018–2019.

The daily topical sentiment indices are available for download.

item.title: Modeling Latent Variables in Economics and Finance
item.description: Supervised by David Ardia and Kris Boudt.
